title: Tokenflow handshake and tooling resilience audit
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Audit and harden the end-to-end token and context handoff between primary and fallback model families as part of smart routing. Goal: eliminate silent failures and subtle output drift when requests are routed across region/tier fallbacks. Work spans tokenizer normalization, prefix/KV cache continuity, streaming/tooling contract compatibility, CI checks, and rollout gating. Deliverables: a small verification harness, updated tooling adapters, CI gates, and a documented runbook for on-call and release engineers.
acceptance_criteria: Round-trip tokenizer parity check added to CI for all supported model families (pass threshold >= 99.9% token id mapping for overlapping vocab subsets)
KV cache continuity tests exercising 1k+ token prefixes across primary->fallback chains with zero panics and <=1% inferred generation divergence in smoke prompts
Tooling contract validation (tool proto/schema) enforced for streaming outputs: schema mismatches produce deterministic fallback to safe-mode and a logged incident
A canary rollout plan and runbook committed to runtime-1.22 release with automated rollback on defined telemetry signals
At least one cross-region simulated failover performed and results filed in this ticket
steps: Inventory current model family descriptors and tooling adapters (manifest versions, tokenizer types, special token sets)
Build a lightweight tokenflow harness that runs tokenizer round-trips, offset mapping, and BPE vs SentencePiece normalization with representative corpora
Add KV-cache continuity integration test: spin primary runtime + simulated fallback runtime and assert cache key invariants across handoff
Implement tooling shim checks: verify tool call shapes and response schemas at handshake time; add strict-mode toggle for safer fallbacks
Wire telemetry: tokenflow_mismatch, kv_handoff_latency, tool_schema_mismatch metrics and a sample dashboard for canary monitoring
Create CI jobs that run the harness on every model manifest change and block merges on regressions
Draft canary rollout doc with smoke tests and rollback triggers; rehearse in staging and capture screenshots/logs
comments: 2026-03-01 Aisha Khan: Initial ticket created after incident review where cross-region fallback produced truncated tool outputs. Proposed scope is limited to handshake and tooling resilience rather than a full tokenizer rewrite.

2026-03-03 Marco Diaz: Completed manifest inventory. Found three families with mixed tokenizer types: bpe-lite, sentencepiece-v2, and a legacy whitespace tokenizer used only by internal experimental models. Proposing to exclude experimental models from immediate CI enforcement.

2026-03-05 Priya Natarajan (SRE): KV cache continuity harness needs ephemeral GPU quota for 2 staging clusters; requested quota increase from infra. Also noted that current KV keys include model-version hashes which will break handoff unless we canonicalize the key schema.

2026-03-07 Marco Diaz: Opened PR to add tokenizer round-trip harness and a small mapping shim for special tokens. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3456. Initial CI run failed on 2 tokens for model family X due to different padding token ids.

2026-03-09 Aisha Khan: Decided on mitigation: introduce canonical token aliasing table at runtime startup and add a pre-handshake normalization step. Security flagged to review alias table persistence and KMS access for any seeded mappings.

2026-03-10 Marco Diaz: Added telemetry stubs for tokenflow_mismatch and tool_schema_mismatch. Next: complete KV continuity test and rehearse cross-region failover in staging week of 2026-03-15. Assigned follow-ups to infra and QA.
